create.name: Simon Cox
create.bio:
Simon Cox is a teacher of Wudang martial arts and a scholar of religion. After a degree in classics from the University of Houston, he moved to China at twenty-one and spent six years at Wudang Mountain under Master Yuan Xiugang, one of twelve foreign students in an intensive five-year programme in the Sanfeng lineage that combined morning qigong, a full day of kung fu and evening meditation or chanting. He went on to a PhD in religion at Rice University with Jeffrey Kripal and Anne Klein, later published by Oxford University Press as The Subtle Body: A Genealogy, a history of the idea of a body of subtle energy in Western thought.

Since 2022 he and his wife Brandi have run Okanagan Valley Wudang in Penticton, British Columbia, treating kung fu, tai chi and qigong together as one path of cultivation, with morning tai chi and qigong classes alongside longer evening sessions. He holds a research fellowship with Esalen's Center for Theory and Research, working with co-founder Michael Murphy on a book about the institute's history, and a visiting scholar at Harvard Divinity School. At Esalen he also teaches Daoist sleep and dream practices drawn from his Wudang training.

books.title: The Subtle Body: A Genealogy
books.author: Simon Cox
books.description: An academic history of the subtle body, the idea of an invisible, energetic body alongside the physical one, as it developed in Western philosophy and esoteric thought. Published by Oxford University Press in its series on Western esotericism, it grew out of his doctoral research at Rice University.

courses.title: Sleep Alchemy: Secrets of Daoist Sleep Practices for Inner Peace and Renewal
courses.description: A five-day Esalen workshop on Wudang sleeping methods such as Hibernating Dragon and Five Dragons Sleeping, which treat rest as a practice of subtle awareness. Classic Daoist dream stories and everyday habits are discussed alongside the practice, in a relaxed and often humorous setting.

courses.title: Tai Chi Classes
courses.description: Weekly Wudang tai chi classes at the school in Penticton, from short Sunday and Wednesday morning sessions on the 9- and 28-posture forms to a twice-weekly evening immersion covering the full curriculum and push hands. Billed as monthly subscriptions.

courses.title: Qigong Classes
courses.description: Sunday and Wednesday morning qigong in Penticton, rotating through seasonal sets including Eight Brocades and Five Animal Frolics. Classes can be taken on their own or combined with tai chi.
